scope: Local correctness and V8 main-thread attribution of stronger JS plus batch Rust composition; no added speedup claim.
limitations: V8 main-thread attribution only: this is not a wall-time speedup, cold-build, Vite/HMR, memory or runtime acceptance experiment.
Each corpus/variant uses a fresh worker; initial compile plus 14 warmups precede 20 independent inspector windows at 1000 microseconds.
Only compileVueFile is inside the requested window; inspector start/stop plumbing and asynchronous continuation can still appear in samples.
Input hashing, metrics, output serialization/comparison and profile writes are outside sampling. Between-call work can still perturb GC and scheduling.
Every initial, warmup and sampled output is checked in full inside each worker, then its digest is checked against the original compiler by the collector.
Loader controls and diagnostic counters remain inside compilation. Variant order is fixed, not randomized or suitable for paired timing inference.
Merged trees provide counts only, without a synthetic timeline. GC, idle and unattributed samples stay in the denominator; inclusive shares overlap.
V8 sampling does not provide Rust/native internal stacks, every process thread, process CPU duration or sourcemap-resolved original locations.
Raw profiles and complete worker outputs remain private; this summary is sanitized separately from the exact byte comparisons and hashes.
Source/binary hashes do not identify every installed dependency file or prove the binary build provenance. Shared-machine contention is not controlled.
interpretation: Five variants compose the existing script JS experiment with binding control/summary/native; no production compiler or Rust source was changed by this round.
All 450 correctness calls and 525 initial/warm/sample calls preserve original compiler output, including maps, warnings and public errors.
Each representative native compilation consumes its binding batch through one addon call; samples have no native fallback or ownership residue.
Raw profile windows and hashes are separately retained; a profile count is not a repeated wall-time sample count.
Local machine contention and visible inspector overhead limit the strength of attribution, especially the smallest Wevu corpus; independent CI evidence remains pending.
transformScript remains a meaningful candidate boundary, but these samples do not establish a complete Rust stage implementation, hit rate, byte/map equivalence or performance.

definitions.compileScriptPhaseInclusive: Any frame at compileVueFile/script.ts named compileScriptPhase; each sample counted once.
definitions.templateIncludingBindingInclusive: Union of compiler/template.ts or compiler/template/**, compileVueFile/template.ts and bindingAnalysisInclusive.
definitions.bindingAnalysisInclusive: Union of production template/bindingManifest.ts, diagnostic nativeBindingAnalysis/compileBatch/**, source.ts, summary.ts, and optimized execution analyzeBindingExpressionsNative wrapper. This includes JS planning and boundary work, not Rust internal stacks.
definitions.babelSelf: Sample leaf belongs to @babel/parser, @babel/traverse or @babel/generator module respectively.
definitions.visibleProfilerOverheadUnion: Union of any inspector/inspector-promises frame and a sample leaf in cpu.ts/cpuWorker.ts/cpuWorkload.ts; visible sampled plumbing, not a causal overhead estimate.
definitions.denominator: All raw samples including GC, idle, inspector and unattributed; inclusive categories overlap and must not be summed.

limitations: Independent Python rehash and sample-stack reconstruction, without invoking compiler or collecting new performance samples.
One loaded shared macOS arm64 machine, fixed variant order and only 20 profiles per cell; no speedup, stable timing or OS comparison follows.
All 525 per-call outputs were compared by digest to baseline complete output bytes; only first full worker output is retained and compared byte-for-byte.
Profile intervals include inspector plumbing and async continuation. Counts are unweighted samples, not wall time or process CPU time.
Profiler overhead fraction only includes visible sampled stack plumbing; instrumentation impact on compilation/GC/scheduling is not causally measured.
Source identities cover 269 named files, not every installed dependency; matching binary bytes do not establish build provenance.
No Rust internal stacks, worker/process threads, HMR, cold-build, memory or runtime acceptance.
